source_snapshot.procedure: Run `openbmctool.py ... ldap privilege-mapper create --groupName=<groupName> --privilege="priv-admin/priv-user"` after generic prechecks/log clearing.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL preserves the create action and inputs but uses credential-bearing connection syntax, treats output/HTTP status as proof, does not choose or independently preserve the `priv-admin` and `priv-user` variants, and omits group canonicalization, collision checks, effective authorization and cleanup.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION with CRITICAL risk correctly requires a pinned tool, exact group DN/CN and nesting semantics, a dedicated non-production group/user, complete mapping baseline, one least-privilege create, mapped/control-user authorization, local recovery and cleanup.

old_problem: The source's slash-separated `priv-admin/priv-user` must be bound to actual independent role variants rather than copied literally or guessed. Command success cannot prove canonical group matching, persistent mapping, effective permissions, denial boundaries, lack of collision or cleanup. Exact directory identities and Project authorization matrices were previously treated as pending inputs even though they can be parameterized safely.
disposition_reason: The documented openbmctool create semantics are sufficient to define an engineer-reviewable test. Preserve both source privilege choices as separately identified variants; bind canonical groups, users and allowed/denied operations at runtime; create only one isolated mapping per approval; verify persisted and effective authorization; remove it and reconcile the baseline before any second variant. Missing group names and role matrices are Project configuration, not unresolved engineering logic.
decision_basis: XLSX row 930, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, adjacent Delete-Mapping row and preserved V3.1 record were directly reviewed; row 931 and its manifest identity were independently verified.

Pinned openbmctool documentation defines the privilege-mapper create command and separate delete/list operations and documents `priv-admin` and `priv-user` role values. This supports a bounded create/readback/effective-auth/cleanup contract without guessing an OEM payload.

OpenBMC user-management architecture explains that LDAP groups map into BMC privilege roles and that authorization is interface/channel dependent; a stored mapping alone therefore cannot be the PASS criterion.

ED-02/ED-21/ED-26 reusable identity principles prohibit collapsing distinct coverage, while ED-03/ED-13 and ED-33 through ED-38 allow runtime binding but preserve approval, recovery and engineer-owned execution verdict.

test_case.test_name: Create and verify isolated LDAP group mappings for each required priv-user and priv-admin source variant
test_case.purpose: Verify independently for every Project-required source role variant that a pinned openbmctool creates exactly one approved canonical LDAP-group-to-BMC-role mapping, persists it without changing any other mapping, grants a dedicated member only the expected permissions, denies disallowed/control access, preserves local recovery and removes the test mapping cleanly.
required_package: Target BMC/firmware identity, supported role schema and pinned reviewed openbmctool/openbmc-tools commit
Coverage matrix retaining separate `priv-user` and `priv-admin` rows; each row has an explicit required/not-applicable decision backed by Project access-control policy
For each executed row, a unique non-production canonical LDAP group identity/realm/case/nesting rule and dedicated mapped member plus unmapped/control user
Role-specific non-destructive allow/deny matrix for WebUI/Redfish/SSH or other supported interfaces, including channel restrictions
Complete redacted pre-state of mappings, LDAP config, accounts, roles and named sessions plus collision/duplicate check
Protected BMC/test credentials, independent local-admin/console recovery, one-create approval and exact named-mapping cleanup/restore plan
test_case.test_command: CRITICAL AUTHORIZATION CHANGE; DO NOT EXECUTE WITHOUT PER-VARIANT APPROVAL. Preserve security logs, pin/review openbmctool and validate the exact target schema. Build separate coverage rows for `priv-user` and `priv-admin`; never pass one from the other. For one approved row only, prove the canonical group and controlled membership, select the literal single role value (never `priv-admin/priv-user`), capture the complete redacted mapping baseline and verify no collision plus local recovery. Create exactly one mapping using protected BMC authentication, then list/read back its exact group and role with an audit event. From independent sessions, test the dedicated mapped user against every approved allowed and denied non-destructive operation, test an unmapped/control user, and confirm local-admin recovery. Delete only the created mapping under the approved cleanup, verify it is absent and every pre-existing mapping is unchanged. Close sessions and rotate test secrets. Repeat another role only after cleanup and separate approval. Do not clear logs or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: For each executed role row, exactly one mapping for the canonical dedicated group persists with the literal approved `priv-user` or `priv-admin` value and no unrelated mapping changes. The dedicated member receives precisely the role's allowed permissions and is denied disallowed actions; the unmapped/control identity does not inherit the mapping; local recovery remains valid. The test mapping is then removed, the baseline mapping set is restored exactly and audit evidence contains no secrets. The two role variants retain separate results.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: A role row passes only with approval, canonical identity/membership evidence, collision-free create, exact persisted mapping, mapped-user allowed and denied effective-authorization results, control-user restriction, local recovery and exact cleanup. Tool output/HTTP status/list appearance alone cannot pass. Wrong or broadened group resolution, privilege escalation, a mapped or control-user authorization mismatch, unrelated mapping change, secret exposure, local lockout, cleanup failure or residual test mapping is FAIL and stops. Missing group/role matrix/tool/recovery/approval is NOT READY. Overall source PASS requires every Project-required source role row to pass; a role may be N/A only with authoritative Project scope evidence.
safety_gate: Never use a production group/user or grant administrator privilege merely for convenience; `priv-admin` requires its own named high-risk approval and bounded non-destructive permission checks.
Resolve canonical DN/CN, realm, case, nested-group and membership semantics before creation; stop on ambiguity or an existing collision.
Protect all credentials and directory data; keep secrets out of URLs, command history, process listings, logs, screenshots and records.
Create one mapping at a time, verify local/console recovery, and remove it before another role. Never bulk-edit mappings or clear security logs.
Stop on unexpected privilege, duplicate mapping, cross-group access, local-access impact or cleanup failure; preserve evidence and do not retry or grant a higher role to debug.
expected_evidence: Per-role coverage matrix, approvals, target/firmware, pinned tool commit/hash and authoritative BMC role/interface semantics
Canonical dedicated group/realm/case/nesting/membership proof, mapped and control identities, and complete redacted baseline with collision check
One create response/audit and exact persisted group/role readback for each separately executed role row
Mapped-user allowed/denied effective permission results, unmapped/control-user restrictions and independent local-admin recovery
Exact created-mapping deletion, full baseline equality/no unrelated change, preserved logs/secrets and separate engineer verdict per role
test_case.recovery: On wrong group resolution, privilege, duplicate, authorization result or access impact, stop all further role variants without retry. Use the independent local-admin/console path to delete only the created mapping by its verified identity, restore the full saved mapping baseline if needed, revoke test memberships/sessions, preserve audit evidence and rotate exposed credentials. Escalate if exact cleanup or prior authorization state cannot be proven.

source_conflict.reason: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require adding a privilege mapping. The slash-separated values are documented choices and are preserved as independent parameterized coverage rows rather than a contradictory literal value.

blocked.reason: The create/readback/effective-authorization/cleanup method and safety boundary are defined. Canonical groups, role scope and permission matrices are Project execution inputs.
